choices.english: Whoever does not take up his cross and follow after me is not worthy of me
choices.why: The articular participle Ὃς introduces a universal conditional; λαμβάνει is present active indicative, rendered as 'take up' to convey the ongoing assumption of the cross; ἀκολουθεῖ is present active, 'follow after' preserves the sequential sense; the double negation with οὐκ ἔστι μου ἄξιος is idiomatically rendered as 'is not worthy of me'

pass_b_english: And yet Paul cries out, 'Be steadfast, immovable!' But the Lord himself, in his most approachable and persuasive manner, sets the highest value on those who possess anything, only to meet with slander. He draws a boundary against the disease of turning away.

For he said of certain ones, 'They loved to move their feet and did not spare themselves, and God did not approve in them.' For what is firmly and immovably established toward anything useful is safe and inviolable. Indeed, the blood of animals is brought forth, and so on.

But there are also many other words about these matters; however, let them pass by now because of their multitude. Nevertheless, Christ died according to the flesh, that he might cleanse us by his own blood.
Therefore we go forth to him. Let us then bear his reproach, that is, the cross on our behalf. Thus he also said, 'Whoever does not take up his cross and follow after me is not worthy of me.'
